purpose: Tighten the GitHub Actions pinning ratchet from 1028 to the 1026 floating references actually present - the tool itself reported the slack - and make the pinned count an enforced floor instead of a decorative field. pinnedReferences was written by --update-baseline and never read by any check, so it asserted nothing.
requiredInvariants: No workflow file changes. Not a single action is pinned or unpinned in this pass: the ratchet records and enforces the state that already exists.
The ceiling is only lowered to the measured 1026, never raised. Floating branches remain an unconditional failure.

The pass does NOT claim actions are pinned. 1026 floating references remain and the tool keeps printing that this is not such a claim; historical debt is unchanged and still tracked in SUPPLY_CHAIN_MATRIX.md.

The pinnedReferences jump from 8 to 64 recorded by --update-baseline is NOT presented as a control gained in this pass. Those 56 actions were pinned by earlier work; the field simply had never been read. What is new is that the number is now enforced.
Missing or non-integer pinnedReferences fails closed, matching how maxFloatingReferences is already treated, so the floor cannot be disabled by deleting a field.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No schema change, no migration, no dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: The slack was reported by the tool, not guessed: 'floating references fell to 1026; run --update-baseline to tighten the ratchet.'

The gap the floor closes is narrow and was proven rather than argued. Unpinning a single action raises floating and lowers pinned, so the ceiling alone catches it. Unpinning one action WHILE deleting another floating reference leaves floating at exactly 1026 - on the ceiling - and lowers pinned to 63.
Both versions of the checker were run against that identical mutated tree: the old ceiling-only code printed WITHIN_BASELINE and exited 0; the new code failed closed naming the fall from 64 to 63.
Three further mutations, all caught: pinned floor raised by one; pinnedReferences set to a non-integer; pinnedReferences deleted outright. The last two fail closed rather than skipping the check.
Clean tree afterwards: the workflow edits used to construct the proof were reverted, leaving only the baseline and the checker modified.
